name: The Hunger Games
description: Defiance, survival and the cost of spectacle, from Panem.
author: Quips Editorial

quotes.content: Happy Hunger Games! And may the odds be ever in your favor!
quotes.notes: Effie's reaping-day benediction, delivered brightly to children about to be drawn for a fight to the death; the US editions read favor, not favour.

quotes.content: I volunteer! I volunteer as tribute!
quotes.notes: Katniss steps forward in her sister Prim's place at the District 12 reaping; the novel sets the two sentences apart with the tag “I gasp.”

quotes.content: District Twelve. Where you can starve to death in safety.
quotes.notes: Katniss's summary of her home district in the novel's opening pages.

quotes.content: Here's some advice. Stay alive.
quotes.notes: Haymitch's entire mentoring strategy, offered drunk on the train to the Capitol.

quotes.content: I always channel my emotions into my work. That way, I don't hurt anyone but myself.
quotes.notes: Cinna on why he pours what he feels into his designs rather than into open defiance.

quotes.content: I am not pretty. I am not beautiful. I am as radiant as the sun.
quotes.notes: Katniss seeing what Cinna has made of her before the pre-Games interview.

quotes.content: I don't want them to change me in there. Turn me into some kind of monster that I'm not.
quotes.notes: Peeta on the roof the night before the Games, trying to name something the Capitol cannot take.

quotes.content: You don't forget the face of the person who was your last hope.
quotes.notes: Katniss on Peeta, who took a beating to throw her burnt bread the winter her family was starving.

quotes.content: I want to do something, right here, right now, to shame them, to make them accountable, to show the Capitol that whatever they do or force us to do there is a part of every tribute they can't own. That Rue was more than a piece in their Games. And so am I.
quotes.notes: Katniss covering Rue's body in flowers — the small act of refusal the rebellion later grows from.

quotes.content: Katniss, the girl who was on fire.
quotes.notes: Attribution axis fails: the phrase is Cinna's coinage and recurs across the trilogy, so the speaker and placement of this particular instance need checking against the novel.

quotes.content: I think we'll make this whole thing a lot simpler by agreeing not to lie to each other.
quotes.notes: Snow opening his unannounced visit to Katniss's house in District 12.

quotes.content: It's the things we love most that destroy us.
quotes.notes: Snow's theory of leverage, offered to Katniss as a warning about everyone she would protect.

quotes.content: It must be very fragile, if a handful of berries can bring it down.
quotes.notes: Katniss's answer to Snow's claim that her stunt in the arena threatened the whole Capitol.

quotes.content: Remember who the real enemy is.
quotes.notes: Haymitch's last instruction before the Quarter Quell, which Katniss does not understand until the arena breaks open.

quotes.content: You could live a hundred lifetimes and not deserve him, you know.
quotes.notes: Haymitch's verdict on Peeta, delivered to Katniss without softening.

quotes.content: They can't hurt me. There's no one left I love.
quotes.notes: Wording axis fails: Johanna's phrasing here is recalled rather than checked, and it circulates in several variant forms.

quotes.content: Fire is catching! And if we burn, you burn with us!
quotes.notes: Katniss's unscripted line to the camera after the Capitol bombs a hospital full of wounded in District 8.

quotes.content: You love me. Real or not real?
quotes.notes: The recovery game Peeta uses after the Capitol's hijacking left him unable to sort his own memories from planted ones; Katniss answers, Real.

quotes.content: Destroying things is much easier than making them.
quotes.notes: Wording axis holds but attribution does not: whether this falls in Katniss's narration or in her dialogue needs checking against the novel.

quotes.content: It takes ten times as long to put yourself back together as it does to fall apart.
quotes.notes: Attribution axis fails: the line is usually given to Finnick, but whether he or Katniss speaks it needs checking against the novel.

quotes.content: Closing my eyes doesn't help. Fire burns brighter in the darkness.
quotes.notes: Katniss on the nightmares that follow her out of the arena and do not stop when the Games do.

quotes.content: Something is significantly wrong with a creature that sacrifices its children's lives to settle its differences.
quotes.notes: Katniss's verdict near the end of the trilogy, aimed at the Games and the war that replaced them alike.

quotes.content: I no longer feel any allegiance to these monsters called human beings, despite being one myself.
quotes.notes: Katniss after Prim's death, refusing to exempt herself from the judgment she is passing.

quotes.content: What I need is the dandelion in the spring. The bright yellow that means rebirth instead of destruction. The promise that life can go on, no matter how bad our losses. That it can be good again.
quotes.notes: The closing pages: what Katniss decides she needs to survive, set against Gale's fire.

quotes.content: That's when I make a list in my head of every act of goodness I've seen someone do. It's like a game. Repetitive. Even a little tedious after more than twenty years. But there are much worse games to play.
quotes.notes: The last lines of the trilogy, on the game Katniss plays instead of the one Panem made her play.

quotes.content: Katniss will pick whoever she thinks she can't survive without.
quotes.notes: Gale's answer to Peeta when the two of them work out, between themselves, where they stand.

quotes.content: Hope is the only thing stronger than fear.
quotes.notes: Film-only line, spoken by Snow to Seneca Crane and absent from the novel; the exact wording needs checking against the film, which cannot be rewatched here.

quotes.content: Snow lands on top.
quotes.source: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes (2020)
quotes.notes: The Snow family refrain, repeated through the novel by the impoverished boy who will become President Snow.

quotes.content: The upside of being born on reaping day is that you can sleep late on your birthday. It's pretty much downhill from there.
quotes.notes: The novel's opening lines, from the first chapter Scholastic released as an authorized pre-publication excerpt.

quotes.content: Because the reaping's going to happen no matter what I believe. Sure as the sun will rise tomorrow.
quotes.notes: Haymitch on the day's inevitability, page 10; the line the novel's title answers.

quotes.content: Don't let them use you, Sarshee. Don't let them paint their posters with your blood. Not if you can help it.
quotes.notes: Advice given to an earlier tribute, reaching Haymitch through his mother and repeated to himself on page 49.

quotes.content: I don't think we 'submit.'
quotes.notes: Page 104; the inner single quotes are the novel's, marking the Capitol's word being handed back to it.

quotes.content: And I will orchestrate your death based on your behavior from here on out.
quotes.notes: Snow setting the terms on page 130, in the flat register he reserves for threats.

quotes.content: Maybe one day. But we can't any of us do it alone.
quotes.notes: The novel's closing note on page 377, and the answer to the isolation Haymitch spends the book learning.
